title: Correlative Geometric--Molecular--Force Metrology for Chemical Control of Nanoscale Film Stability
topic: How can microscopic and nanoscale interfacial phenomena be measured beyond film thickness alone?

source.evidence_use: The cited Survey anchors support the component capabilities of geometry, interface-specific spectroscopy, confined-force characterization, and nanoscale film measurement. They do not establish the proposed cross-modality causal relation or show that a chemistry-mediated disjoining-pressure mechanism has already been observed.

directions.title: Correlative Geometric--Molecular--Force Metrology for Chemical Control of Nanoscale Film Stability
directions.abstract: Thickness is necessary but insufficient evidence for microscopic interfacial mechanism. This selected idea proposes a bounded, non-biological liquid--solid thin-film research object in which geometry, interface-specific molecular state, and local confined-force response are treated as complementary state representations. The causal proposition is not that a chosen measurement channel proves a mechanism by itself. Instead, under a qualified geometry-matched comparison boundary, molecular-state and confined-force transitions must both add explanatory value and display a defensible temporal relation to film drainage, arrest, stability, or rupture beyond a geometry-only account. Calibration, surface history, probe perturbation, model dependence, and time-registration uncertainty are first-class alternatives. The intended contribution is an evidence architecture that makes chemistry-mediated disjoining-pressure control testable rather than inferred from thickness alone.

hypothesis.central_hypothesis: Within a bounded non-biological liquid--solid thin-film system, a temporally coherent relation among film geometry, an interface-specific vibrational state, and a confined-force proxy can distinguish chemistry-mediated disjoining-pressure control of drainage or stability from a thickness-only explanation.

scientific_object.geometric_component: Time-varying film thickness, curvature, and/or morphology at a liquid--solid boundary.
scientific_object.molecular_component: An interface-specific vibrational or chemical-state representation, interpreted with its model limits.
scientific_object.mechanical_component: A local confined-force or disjoining-pressure proxy, interpreted with its perturbation and interaction-model limits.
scientific_object.target_relation: molecular interfacial state -> local confined interaction or disjoining-pressure contribution -> drainage or stability transition, conditional on matched geometry

hypothesis.mechanism_or_relation: Molecular reorganization or adsorption at the liquid--solid interface changes the local interaction landscape and therefore its disjoining-pressure contribution. A mechanism-consistent account requires that molecular-state and local-force representations contribute explanatory information beyond geometry and relate coherently to the declared stability transition.
hypothesis.intervention_or_transformation: At the research-design level, compare expert-approved geometry-matched interface states and assess whether geometry alone explains the declared transition or whether the molecular-state and confined-force representations provide additional coherent discrimination. The Idea stage specifies no material identity, chemical identity, instrument configuration, numerical parameter, or operational procedure.
hypothesis.expected_mechanism: A chemistry-mediated change should manifest as a state-dependent relation across the three representations: the molecular signal and local-force proxy change in a manner consistent with a changed interaction landscape, and their relation to drainage or stability cannot be reduced to film geometry alone.
hypothesis.discriminating_observation: Relative to a geometry-only account, a model that includes the interface-specific molecular-state and confined-force representations explains a declared stability transition more consistently across comparable observations, with a temporal relation that survives calibration, surface-history, perturbation, and alignment uncertainty assessment.
hypothesis.evidence_requirement: Retain time-resolved geometry, an interface-specific molecular representation, a local confined-force representation, a declared transition outcome, a common comparability boundary, and explicit uncertainty/perturbation records. Interpret a cross-channel association as mechanism evidence only when it discriminates against named alternatives rather than merely co-occurs with thickness change.
evidence_basis: The Survey identifies nonlinear optical spectroscopy as a source of interface-specific molecular and orientational constraints (R2--R4).
The Survey identifies AFM/SFA-type observations as sources of local morphology and confined-force evidence, with perturbation and model limitations (R9--R10).
The Survey identifies ellipsometric imaging as a geometric anchor for nanometer-scale liquid films (R11).
The proposed time-aligned three-channel causal discrimination is a new hypothesis. No source anchor is treated as direct proof of the combined relation.
hypothesis.boundary_or_failure_condition: The claim fails or is narrowed when a geometry-only account explains the outcome equally well; molecular and force channels do not add coherent discriminating information; or calibration, surface history, capillarity, probe effects, roughness, interaction-model error, measurement-induced chemistry, or temporal mismatch explains the apparent relation.
hypothesis.claim_scope: Only an expert-approved, non-biological liquid--solid nanoscale thin-film comparison with declared geometry, calibration, and uncertainty boundaries. The idea does not claim a universal interface law, application performance, or a demonstrated chemical mechanism.
assumptions: A comparable geometrical state can be declared across the observations without asserting perfect equivalence.
The molecular and local-force channels can be interpreted with stated uncertainty instead of being treated as direct unqualified observables.
Qualified domain experts can select an appropriate non-biological model system and decide whether a physical study is suitable.

gap_alignment.statement: Optical thickness alone does not identify molecular orientation, chemical state, local force, or the cause of a transport or stability transition.
Complementary modalities have distinct spatial, temporal, and interpretive limits; an unqualified correlation across channels cannot establish an interfacial mechanism.
Calibration assumptions, surface history, probe effects, roughness, interaction models, and measurement-induced chemistry can all create non-mechanistic explanations.

trace.scientific_concern: A change in film thickness or stability can be generated by geometry, capillarity, surface history, or measurement artifacts without a chemistry-mediated disjoining-pressure mechanism.
trace.required_revision: Require an explicit geometry-only comparator and retain molecular-state, local-force, calibration, surface-history, probe-perturbation, interaction-model, and temporal-alignment alternatives in the evidence record.
alternative_explanations: Geometry, curvature, or capillary forcing explains the transition.
Optical calibration or refractive-index assumptions generate the apparent relation.
Surface history, contamination, or roughness changes the interface state.
The local probe, its interaction model, or the observation modality perturbs the interface.
Channel-registration uncertainty creates apparent precedence or correlation.
trace.final_scope: A bounded, non-biological liquid--solid thin-film mechanism-discrimination claim, not a universal theory or an already demonstrated experimental result.

experiment_handoff.claim_to_test: Within a bounded non-biological liquid--solid thin-film system, a temporally coherent relation among film geometry, an interface-specific vibrational state, and a confined-force proxy can distinguish chemistry-mediated disjoining-pressure control of drainage or stability from a thickness-only explanation.

gap_records.statement: Thickness-only representations cannot identify the molecular state or confined interaction responsible for an observed transition.
gap_records.why_it_matters: The proposed mechanism must add explanatory evidence beyond geometric observation.

gap_records.statement: Different measurement channels can observe related states at incompatible scales or times.
gap_records.why_it_matters: Without explicit alignment and uncertainty, cross-channel correlation cannot discriminate a causal relation.

gap_records.statement: Optical models, surface history, probes, roughness, and measurement-induced changes can mimic a mechanism.
gap_records.why_it_matters: A design must retain these explanations as explicit failure paths rather than post hoc caveats.

scientific_object.description: An expert-approved, non-biological liquid--solid thin-film interface considered through geometric, interface-specific molecular, and local confined-interaction state representations.

experiment_handoff.mechanism_to_discriminate: Molecular reorganization or adsorption changes the local interaction landscape and its disjoining-pressure contribution, thereby contributing to drainage or stability beyond an account based only on geometry.
experiment_handoff.claim_scope: A declared, expert-approved model interface and geometry-matched comparison boundary only. The handoff proposes no physical implementation and does not claim that the mechanism is already established.
assumptions: A suitable non-biological model interface can be selected only after expert review of scientific relevance, safety, compatibility, and calibration traceability.
Comparable states can be declared across geometry, molecular, and force representations with their limitations documented.
The downstream design can distinguish a temporal relation from a coincidental sequence.
boundary_conditions: No material identity, chemical identity, apparatus choice, numerical parameter, or procedural sequence is supplied here.
All selection of model system, materials, chemical handling, facility constraints, calibration strategy, and operational feasibility remains needs_human_input.
The work is non-biological and must remain within institutionally approved physical and chemical safety boundaries.
No stability, transport, or molecular-state result is inferred without an explicit geometry-only comparison and uncertainty audit.
alternative_explanations: Geometry, curvature, or capillary forcing alone produces the stability transition.
Optical calibration or refractive-index assumptions misrepresent the geometric state.
Surface history, contamination, or roughness produces the apparent molecular or local-force change.
Probe perturbation, interaction-model error, or measurement-induced chemistry produces the apparent mechanism.
Temporal registration uncertainty creates an apparent causal sequence.
required_observations: A time-resolved geometric representation of film thickness and/or morphology with calibration uncertainty.
An interface-specific vibrational or chemical-state representation with interpretation limits.
A local confined-force or disjoining-pressure representation with perturbation and model limits.
A stated drainage, arrest, persistence, or rupture-transition outcome.
A declared common time basis, comparability boundary, and uncertainty representation.
A geometry-only comparison used to judge whether the added channels truly improve mechanism discrimination.

evidence_roles.expected_role: Supports complementary AFM and optical observation of nanoscale interfacial objects.
evidence_roles.claim_limits: Does not establish chemistry-mediated disjoining-pressure control.

evidence_roles.expected_role: Supports a confined-force and reactivity measurement capability relevant to local interaction hypotheses.

evidence_roles.expected_role: Supports ellipsometric observation of nanometer-scale liquid-film geometry as a component geometric anchor.
evidence_roles.claim_limits: Geometry alone remains insufficient and this anchor does not prove the proposed molecular-plus-force relation.

risks: The proposed molecular and local-force representations may not be sufficiently specific to resolve the mechanism.
Spatial or temporal registration limits may make the observations non-comparable.
Surface-history, roughness, or probe effects may dominate the inferred relation.
A valid conclusion may remain restricted to a single model interface and not extend to applied systems.
known_unknowns: Which expert-approved model interface permits all three observation classes without invalidating their comparability.
Whether the molecular-state and confined-force changes show a defensible temporal ordering.
Whether a geometry-matched comparison can reduce capillary and surface-history alternatives enough for causal discrimination.
Whether the three-channel relation transfers across a second non-biological interface class.

directions.mature_idea: A bounded measurement-science hypothesis that turns thickness-only non-identifiability into a testable geometric--molecular--force evidence architecture for nanoscale liquid-film stability.

source_lineage.contribution: Method capability matrix, thickness-only limitation, cross-validated evidence anchors, and explicit modality limitations.

directions.independence_rationale: The Survey establishes complementary component capabilities and their limitations. This Idea independently combines them into a falsifiable causal-discrimination architecture with required temporal registration and alternative-explanation auditing; it does not represent that combination as a reported literature result.

directions.title: Multimodal State Map for Nanoscale Evaporation and Interfacial Thermal Resistance
directions.abstract: A retained direction in which geometric, molecular-state, and transport representations would test whether an interfacial state change explains nanoscale evaporative transport beyond liquid distribution or bulk heating. It is not selected because the supplied Survey contains a less direct cross-validated evidence cluster connecting all channels in one evaporative regime.
directions.falsifier: The transport response is fully explained by geometry or bulk heating after the declared alternatives are considered.

directions.title: Cross-Modality Artifact Discrimination for Nanoscale Liquid--Solid Interface Dynamics
directions.abstract: A retained methodological direction in which a dynamic liquid-cell observation would require corroboration by a lower-perturbation representation within a declared comparability boundary. It is not selected because part of the upstream liquid-phase electron microscopy evidence is OpenAlex-only discovery evidence.
directions.falsifier: A lower-perturbation representation does not reproduce the relevant transition after comparability and perturbation differences are assessed.

legacy_best_entry.title: Correlative Geometric--Molecular--Force Metrology for Chemical Control of Nanoscale Film Stability
legacy_best_entry.abstract: A non-biological, design-level hypothesis that evaluates whether time-aligned geometry, molecular-state, and confined-force evidence can discriminate chemistry-mediated nanoscale film stability from a thickness-only explanation.
legacy_best_entry.central_hypothesis: Within a bounded non-biological liquid--solid thin-film system, a temporally coherent relation among film geometry, an interface-specific vibrational state, and a confined-force proxy can distinguish chemistry-mediated disjoining-pressure control of drainage or stability from a thickness-only explanation.

scientific_object.target_relation: molecular interfacial state -> confined interaction contribution -> drainage or stability transition, conditional on matched geometry

legacy_best_entry.mechanism_or_relation: Molecular reorganization or adsorption changes the local interaction landscape and its disjoining-pressure contribution beyond what geometry alone identifies.
legacy_best_entry.intervention_or_transformation: Conceptually compare geometry-matched interface states without selecting materials, chemical identities, hardware, parameters, or a procedure.
legacy_best_entry.discriminating_observation: Molecular-state and local-force representations add temporally coherent discriminating information beyond a geometry-only account.
